description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario unido para resolver el desafío de identificar análogos terrestres de las bases lunares permanentes y de Marte. Cada integrante aporta una especialidad distinta, desde la interpretación científica de datos hasta el desarrollo de herramientas y la comunicación de resultados. Buscamos transformar datos abiertos de NASA y otras agencias en un mapa interactivo que ayude a las futuras misiones a probar equipos y estrategias en la Tierra antes de viajar.
summary:
Earth's Twins is an interactive platform designed to identify and compare locations on Earth that resemble potential sites on the Moon and Mars.

Our solution integrates 3D planetary models, allowing users to select points of interest on the Moon or Mars and discover their corresponding analog locations on Earth. Each location provides valuable information, including geographic coordinates, elevation, terrain characteristics, geological composition, minerals, environmental conditions, temperature and precipitation cycles, as well as its suitability for research and equipment testing. It also highlights the limitations of each analogy, operational advantages, and data sources.

By leveraging NASA data and scientific information, our platform makes planetary comparisons more accessible and intuitive, helping researchers explore a wider range of terrestrial environments for testing.

Earth's Twins addresses the challenge of finding reliable Earth-based analogs for future space exploration. By expanding research and field-testing opportunities, our project contributes to better preparation, more informed decision-making, and safer future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
What it does and how it works

Earth's Twins is an interactive platform developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It features interactive 3D models of Earth, Mars, and the Moon, allowing users to rotate, zoom in, and explore each planetary body. Users can select predefined points of interest on Mars or the Moon and discover their corresponding analog locations on Earth.

Currently, the platform includes four selected terrestrial locations: Mina de Oro and Inti Huasi, both in La Carolina, San Luis, Argentina; Laguna Colorada, near Potosí, Bolivia; and the Chicxulub Crater, in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula.

Each location provides a comprehensive information profile, including geographic coordinates, elevation, terrain characteristics, geological composition, mineral resources, environmental conditions, monthly and anual temperature and precipitation patterns, and diurnal cycle references. It also evaluates suitability for scientific research and equipment testing, identifies where the analogy differs, and presents operational advantages, limitations, and data sources.

Benefits and target use

Our platform is primarily designed for scientists and researchers working in planetary science and space exploration. Its main benefit is bringing relevant scientific information together in a single, accessible profile, simplifying the search for and comparison of terrestrial analog environments. This reduces the need to consult multiple sources separately and makes it easier to evaluate potential research and testing locations.

Expected impact

Earth's Twins aims to expand the number of terrestrial locations available for research and field testing. By identifying environments that share relevant characteristics with the Moon and Mars, researchers may have more opportunities to test equipment, evaluate technologies, and prepare for future space missions before deploying them beyond Earth.

Creativity and innovation

What makes Earth's Twins different is its scientific approach to planetary analogies. Rather than relying on visual similarities alone, our project considers geological, topographical, mineralogical, and environmental factors. Its innovative feature is combining interactive planetary exploration with detailed scientific information in one platform, connecting extraterrestrial locations with real-world environments that can be simulated on Earth.

Data sources and scientific considerations

Our development was based on scientific reports and information from official NASA sources. Our team considered multiple factors to evaluate the relevance of each analogy, including elevation, terrain, geology, mineral composition, temperature, precipitation, environmental conditions, and operational feasibility.

By bringing these elements together, Earth's Twins seeks to make planetary research more accessible, encourage the discovery of new terrestrial analog sites, and contribute to the preparation of safer and better-informed future missions to the Moon and Mars.
